methods.label: Add the whole and fractional parts
methods.explanation:
Add the whole-number parts first, then use a common denominator of \(60\) for the fractional parts. Calling the sum \(S\), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
S&=(2+3+4+5)+\left(\frac12+\frac13+\frac14+\frac15\right)\\
&=14+\frac{30+20+15+12}{60}\\
&=15+\frac{17}{60}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(0<\frac{17}{60}<1\), the sum lies strictly between \(15\) and \(16\). Thus the smallest whole number larger than the sum is \(16\), choice C.
